trust_decision.summary: Whether an admin/onboarding-supplied MAILER_SMTP_URL is a plain smtp(s)://[user:pass@]host[:port] URL; decided once at write time by validateSMTPUrl via validateEnvValues, whose host group [^:]+ lets path/query through, so nodemailer's URL option parsing (e.g. a sendmail transport switch) is reached when the raw string is passed as transport.

landing_point.why: Summary names MAILER_SMTP_URL; the only validator for that key is validateSMTPUrl with its permissive regex at line 209.

fix_sites.entry_point: GraphQL mutation updateInfraConfigs (admin) -> InfraConfigService.updateMany -> validateEnvValues; and REST POST onboarding/config -> updateOnboardingConfig -> validateEnvValues

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the stored-value route: the URL is only ever written by an admin through the validated write paths, so re-checking at mailer start looks redundant and 'not the reported input'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate SMTP URLs with credentials, port and an optional trailing slash (smtp(s)://user:pass@host:587/) must still be accepted, and the separate custom-config object transport (host/port/auth fields) must keep working; an over-broad fix (rejecting '@', '/', or the whole string transport) breaks normal mailer setup.

O6_input_shapes: hostname starting with '.' or empty hostname

O7_producer.where: packages/hoppscotch-backend/src/infra-config/helper.ts:94-118 (loadInfraConfiguration, decrypts DB rows into env.INFRA consumed by packages/hoppscotch-backend/src/mailer/helper.ts:28)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MAILER_SMTP_URL already persisted in infra_config (written before the validator was tightened) is loaded at boot and passed raw to nodemailer without re-validation.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Fix is about rejecting bad input at write time; the stored value came from an admin and the loader is 'just config plumbing'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file (mailer/helper.ts and infra-config/helper.ts) from landing point utils.ts, same backend package

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Custom-config branch built from a stored URL-like MAILER_SMTP_HOST (e.g. 'host:port' string re-parsed via URL) instead of fixed keys, reaching the same option parsing.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MAILER_SMTP_HOST/PORT have only a non-empty check (infra-config.service.ts:799-812); a maintainer adding 'host may include port' convenience would plausibly parse it as a URL.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Adding MAILER_SMTP_URL to the env-file sync list (SYNC_ONLY_VARIABLES at line 15) so the value is written to the DB without passing validateEnvValues.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The sync path already writes env values straight to the DB for PROXY_APP_URL with no validation; extending it to mailer settings is a natural self-host feature.

O9_family: argument/option injection via URL-parsed transport config (CWE-77/78; nodemailer connection-URL query options), validator bypass

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + pnpm monorepo, NestJS backend, Jest, Prisma client generation
services: PostgreSQL (only for full app; validator and getTransportOption unit-testable without it)
O10_build.project_tests: packages/hoppscotch-backend/src/infra-config/infra-config.service.spec.ts:358-409 covers validateEnvValues for other mailer keys; no existing MAILER_SMTP_URL / validateSMTPUrl tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a '?'-blocklist or 'sendmail' substring check to the regex in validateSMTPUrl, leaving path/fragment/backslash shapes and the unvalidated load-time consumer open.
